fieldBindings.english: Record the exact identity and obtain local expert food-use advice before counting it as household food.
Confirm exact species with a qualified indigenous nursery. Do not substitute genus-level berry claims for identification.
Keep this as an identified hedge/inventory plant. Seek expert local food-use review before treating berries as household food.
Confirm the exact species and intended hedge use with a local indigenous nursery.
Record planting batches and harvested leaves/fruit separately.
Match this frost-sensitive plant to dry saline/coastal conditions. Its accumulated salts can return to the soil as plants die.
Obtain exact-species seed or plants and assess the bed soil; no regional food cultivar or annual food yield is verified.
SANBI records this tree in east-coast dune forest from Eastern Cape through KwaZulu-Natal, with tolerance of salty sea spray.
Confirm Mimusops afra and lawful nursery provenance. Check current protected-tree collection requirements before taking plants or products from existing trees.
Retain this climber in mapped inventory, but do not count it as normal household food until a qualified local specialist confirms identity, edible part and safe preparation.
SANBI records it across South Africa except Western Cape, in varied habitats.
Resolve food-use and preparation with an experienced local food-plant specialist before buying it as a household crop.
Treat edible-fat preparation as a specialist process requiring local validation.
Use well-drained coastal sand with sun or semi-shade; fruit production needs correctly sexed planting material.
Confirm the exact species and male/female stock with an indigenous nursery. Keep landscape use separate from an unverified household food process.
Confirm the exact mulberry species and that the chosen plant is a fruiting form. Fruit colour alone cannot identify it.
Watch water stress during fruit development and record the actual ripe picking months.
Ask for identified Morus nigra fruiting material with a locally observed season. Do not use a generic black-fruited mulberry or fruitless ornamental as proof of this product.
SANBI records this slow-growing tree in summer and winter rainfall areas, with frost, drought and wind resistance.
Keep its roots away from walls, patios and pools; SANBI notes that they can be aggressive.
Ask for the wild-olive taxon in the catalogue, rather than substituting a commercial olive cultivar. Record actual local picking.
Match the cultivar to table olives or oil. Check drainage, irrigation and winter conditions; humid summer rainfall can bring disease problems.
Pick at the intended green, black or oil stage. Processing and safe kept-stock conditions must be recorded separately.

Mission is a source-backed black-table and oil candidate; Kalamata is for black table olives; Manzanilla and Barouni for green table olives; Frantoio for oil and compatible pollen. Confirm regional fit through SA Olive's registered nurseries.
SANBI describes a spreading pioneer shrub for sun and well-drained soil, including coastal and inland habitats. Leave room for its spread.
Confirm the exact species and local provenance; the checked source gives no named fruit cultivar.
Female palms need suitable male pollen. Record sex, cultivar and pollination management before forecasting fruit.
Check heat, water and rain during ripening. The Hermon trial found uneven ripening and spoilage, so regional success alone does not establish a local crop.
Medjool is documented in the Hermon study. Obtain known fruiting female material and compatible pollen advice; a seedling's sex and eventual fruit quality are not established by its appearance.
Female trees bear nuts and need pollen from suitable male trees. The Prieska reference comes from a dry, irrigated Karoo farm.
Confirm male and female planting material, irrigation and local winter/summer conditions; a February producer reference does not validate a humid coast.
Discuss Shufrah and Ariyeh from the Prieska producer evidence, or Shufra, Ariyeh and Sirora from the Prince Albert project, with a specialist nursery. Select a compatible male and confirm local fit.
Protect young plants from heavy browsing. SANBI reports warm rocky and semi-arid habitats; ground-level goat browsing can prevent vegetative spread and reduce regeneration.
Ask for correctly identified spekboom and record whether it is planted for food, browse or restoration. No measured household leaf yield is supplied.
Keep each cultivar's picking reference separate. The Robertson example used summer irrigation.
Confirm winter chilling, water and the actual planting material before using a reference as a local plan.
Solitaire has a sourced November first-pick reference and named chilling context at Simondium; discuss its local fit with the nursery.
Imperial has a December reference at Robertson. This is a local trial candidate, not advice for frost-free coastal KZN.

Check measured winter chilling, spring frost, drainage and rain near picking. The older KZN guide regarded commercial suitability there as still under trial; a broad climate-zone label does not replace current local advice.
Pollination depends on the selected cultivar. Compatible flowering and pollen sources are separate from early or late fruit ripening.

Regional guide candidates include Bing, Van, Rainier, Burlat and Vista, which generally need compatible pollen partners. It explicitly lists Lapins, Stella and Sweetheart as self-fertile. Minnie Royal, Royal Lee, Royal Dawn and Early Sweet are lower-chill candidates. Confirm current stock, exact rootstock, compatibility and measured local chilling before purchase; this is not a warm-coast recommendation.
Check the named cultivar's winter needs and compatible pollen before planting. Texas Mission is self-incompatible.
Record whether nut weights mean kernels or nuts in shell; these are different quantities.
Texas Mission is a documented SAPO cultivar; its sheet names Nonpareil as pollen partner and describes a high chilling requirement. Confirm local suitability with the nursery.
Record the named cultivar and actual first and last picking months. January and February references are alternatives, not a mixed-orchard calendar for every tree.
Rosemarie Select is a source-backed Western Cape candidate to discuss with the nursery. Ask about December or Packham's Triumph as compatible pollen partners.
For Packham's Triumph, ask about Clapp's Favourite, December or Starkrimson and check local winter conditions.
Confirm exact identity and the intended food preparation with an experienced local adviser.
The South African account describes stream-bank/forest-slope growth and frost resistance; its berries are described as bird food.
Buy exact-species stock for the verified intended use. Do not treat medicinal or wildlife-fruit evidence as a fresh household-food forecast.
Provide climbing support and control its spread where space is limited. SANBI records coastal dunes and forest margins from Western Cape to KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga.
Confirm Rhoicissus digitata; other wild-grape species have different descriptions and cannot supply its dates.
Provide a trellis or other support. Young plants need water until established; SANBI describes later drought tolerance and sun to semi-shade use.
Ask for Rhoicissus tridentata and record local ripe-fruit months. Do not use medicinal or animal root use as food evidence.
Use well-drained soil and adequate water during establishment; avoid waterlogging and root rot.
Record fresh leaves, dried seasoning and essential oil as different products.
Obtain identified healthy rosemary material and local growing advice; no regional culinary-leaf yield variety is verified.
Its natural setting includes dry stream banks in the Little Karoo and drier Eastern and southern Western Cape.
The pods disperse seeds when dry. Record your local seed collection and use; this is not a measured food yield.
Ask for Schotia afra var. afra, with botanical identity confirmed. The source's five-year shade claim is not a first-food age.
SANBI records this frost- and drought-resistant shade tree in Karoo and Kalahari conditions.
Large amounts of its leaves can taint dairy milk, according to SANBI; this is not a ration recommendation.
Ask about male and female plants if fruit is intended. Natural distribution in the source excludes KwaZulu-Natal; broad hardiness is not a local fruit guarantee.
Pick ripe fruit and record drying separately.
This shrub suits exposed coastal gardens and dune stabilisation; confirm local provenance.
Ask an indigenous nursery for exact species and local material. No regional high-yield food cultivar is verified.
Allow fruit to ripen. This drought-resistant shrub can form a hedge; prune to suit the space.
Confirm the exact species with a local indigenous-plant nursery; no tested regional cultivar or quantified yield selection is established.
Record ripe fruit picking and drying separately. No storage duration or fermentation recipe is assigned.
Confirm the exact species and local provenance; the SANBI assessment places it on stony fynbos/karroid slopes of the Northern and Western Cape.
Shelter this coastal tree from direct salt-laden sea wind; SANBI reports salt burn despite its coastal habitat.
Ask a nursery to confirm the species and lawful provenance. Check current collection requirements before taking plants or products from existing trees.
Harvest young leafy tops; wash off sand before cooking.
Use well-drained coastal sand and keep divided plants moist until established.
Obtain correctly identified coastal planting material; record local growth and leaf-picking months because rainy seasons differ across South Africa.
Harvest young shoots for cooking. Record food harvest separately from animal fodder.
Use a sunny, well-drained coastal, fynbos or Karoo position suited to this water-wise pioneer.
Obtain correctly identified local planting material; no named food cultivar or annual kg/plant benchmark is sourced.
Record picking of young flower buds separately from open flowers.
Match the plant to well-drained coastal sandy conditions and its seasonal growth.
Use exact-species nursery identification; no first bud harvest age or food kg/plant benchmark is verified.
Match this fast pioneer to warm, moist eastern/northern conditions; protect damp, shaded seedlings.
Record young-leaf harvest separately from fruit consumed by wildlife.
Use correctly identified local planting material; no named leaf-food cultivar or quantified annual food output is verified.
It tolerates prolonged drought but grows better with regular water. SANBI records its eastern South African distribution.
Ask for Tulbaghia violacea, rather than a plant identified only as wild garlic. Record local leaf and flower picking separately.
Use the planting date to record the rhizome harvest cycle. The Pretoria trial reference is conditional, not a fixed calendar across climates.
Record fresh rhizome and dried spice weights separately; keep edible ginger distinct from ornamental or African ginger species.
Ask a local supplier for healthy, identified Zingiber officinale planting rhizomes; no South African cultivar-specific yield curve is verified.
SANBI records a wide range from frost-free coast to winter-frost regions. Its hooked and straight thorns matter when choosing access routes.
Ask for an identified buffalo-thorn plant suited to local conditions; the checked source supplies no named food cultivar.
